karten.v: What does “operating system” mean?
karten.r: The operating system is the software that manages a computer's hardware, makes it available to the other programs through uniform services and keeps the programs apart from one another.

karten.v: What does “application program” mean?
karten.r: A program that runs under an operating system and performs a task for the user is called an application program, or program for short.

karten.v: What does “kernel mode” mean?
karten.r: In kernel mode, the running program may execute any instruction of the processor.

karten.v: What does “user mode” mean?
karten.r: In user mode, certain instructions are blocked, such as direct access to devices and setting which program may use which part of main memory.

karten.v: What does “privileged instruction” mean?
karten.r: Such a blocked instruction is called a privileged instruction.

karten.v: What does “kernel” mean?
karten.r: The kernel (the core of the system) is the part of the operating system that runs in kernel mode.

karten.v: What does “drivers” mean?
karten.r: The drivers also belong to the kernel: pieces of software that can control a particular device, such as a particular network card or a particular SSD.

karten.v: What does “system call” mean?
karten.r: A system call is a request from a program to the kernel to perform a particular service, for example to open a file, read data or provide memory.

karten.v: What does “distribution” mean?
karten.r: A distribution is a complete operating system that a vendor or a community assembles from the Linux kernel, tools, application programs and default settings and maintains as a whole.

karten.v: What does “package manager” mean?
karten.r: Every distribution comes with a package manager: a program with which you install, update and remove software from the distribution's sources.

karten.v: What does “LTS release” mean?
karten.r: Every two years in April, an LTS release (Long Term Support) appears, for which Canonical supplies security fixes and bug fixes for five years.

karten.v: What does “point release” mean?
karten.r: A number like 26.04.1 denotes a point release: the same system with the fixes collected up to that point and new installation media.

karten.v: The ______ manages the hardware, offers services to the programs and keeps them apart from one another.
karten.r: The operating system manages the hardware, offers services to the programs and keeps them apart from one another.

karten.v: The ______ itself ensures that ordinary programs cannot touch the hardware directly.
karten.r: The processor itself ensures that ordinary programs cannot touch the hardware directly.

karten.v: The ______ is the only part of the system that is allowed to control the hardware directly.
karten.r: The kernel is the only part of the system that is allowed to control the hardware directly.

karten.v: Programs get hardware services only by asking the ______ for them through a system call.
karten.r: Programs get hardware services only by asking the kernel for them through a system call.

karten.v: Strictly speaking, ______ is only the kernel of an operating system.
karten.r: Strictly speaking, Linux is only the kernel of an operating system.

karten.v: ______ is the kernel; a distribution turns it into a complete system.
karten.r: Linux is the kernel; a distribution turns it into a complete system.

karten.v: For a practice system, you choose the current ______, because it receives fixes for five years.
karten.r: For a practice system, you choose the current LTS release, because it receives fixes for five years.

karten.v: What does “terminal” mean?
karten.r: A terminal is a program with a window into which you type commands as text and in which the computer's responses appear as text.

karten.v: WSL 2 is the fastest way, the ______ is the lab and the live USB stick is real Linux on real hardware.
karten.r: WSL 2 is the fastest way, the virtual machine is the lab and the live USB stick is real Linux on real hardware.

karten.v: For programming and the ______, you choose WSL 2, for labs a virtual machine and for real Linux on real hardware the live USB stick.
karten.r: For programming and the command line, you choose WSL 2, for labs a virtual machine and for real Linux on real hardware the live USB stick.

karten.v: The ______ is the window in which you talk to the system in text form; at the end of each way, you open one.
karten.r: The terminal is the window in which you talk to the system in text form; at the end of each way, you open one.

karten.v: What does “virtual machine” mean?
karten.r: A virtual machine (VM) is a computer simulated by software, with its own processor, main memory, storage devices and network card.

karten.v: What does “host” mean?
karten.r: The host is the real computer with the operating system under which the virtual machine runs.

karten.v: What does “guest” mean?
karten.r: The guest is the operating system that runs in the virtual machine.

karten.v: What does “hypervisor” mean?
karten.r: A hypervisor is the software that creates and runs virtual machines.

karten.v: What does “snapshot” mean?
karten.r: A snapshot is a saved state of a virtual machine to which you can return at any time.

karten.v: What does “address” mean?
karten.r: Every device in a network has a number under which others reach it, its address.

karten.v: What does “NAT mode” mean?
karten.r: In NAT mode (Network Address Translation), the hypervisor works like a router for the VM.

karten.v: A ______ is a computer made of software in which a whole operating system runs.
karten.r: A virtual machine is a computer made of software in which a whole operating system runs.

karten.v: The ______ is the real computer, the guest is the system in the VM.
karten.r: The host is the real computer, the guest is the system in the VM.

karten.v: The ______ builds the virtual machines and watches over them.
karten.r: The hypervisor builds the virtual machines and watches over them.

karten.v: With ______, a guest kernel runs directly on the processor, but everything that would affect the real machine ends up with the hypervisor.
karten.r: With hardware virtualization, a guest kernel runs directly on the processor, but everything that would affect the real machine ends up with the hypervisor.

karten.v: A ______ freezes the state of a VM, and restoring it discards everything that came afterward.
karten.r: A snapshot freezes the state of a VM, and restoring it discards everything that came afterward.

karten.v: In ______, the VM gets out onto the network, but nobody gets in from outside.
karten.r: In NAT mode, the VM gets out onto the network, but nobody gets in from outside.

karten.v: What does “Windows Subsystem for Linux” mean?
karten.r: The Windows Subsystem for Linux, version 2 (WSL 2), is a component of Windows that starts a real Linux kernel in a small virtual machine, which Windows itself creates, starts and stops.

karten.v: WSL 2 is a real ______ in a small VM that Windows manages itself.
karten.r: WSL 2 is a real Linux in a small VM that Windows manages itself.

karten.v: wsl -l -v shows which ______ are set up and whether they run under WSL 2.
karten.r: wsl -l -v shows which distributions are set up and whether they run under WSL 2.

karten.v: In the WSL ______, cat /etc/os-release shows the distribution and uname -r shows Microsoft's kernel.
karten.r: In the WSL terminal, cat /etc/os-release shows the distribution and uname -r shows Microsoft's kernel.

karten.v: ______ in WSL finds drive C: under /mnt/c.
karten.r: Linux in WSL finds drive C: under /mnt/c.

karten.v: Windows sees the ______ files in File Explorer under “Linux”; the address is \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-26.04.
karten.r: Windows sees the Linux files in File Explorer under “Linux”; the address is \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-26.04.

karten.v: ______ that you work with in Linux belong in the Linux part, not in /mnt/c.
karten.r: Files that you work with in Linux belong in the Linux part, not in /mnt/c.

karten.v: WSL 2 is ideal for the ______ and programming; for network labs and your own devices, it is too far removed from the hardware.
karten.r: WSL 2 is ideal for the command line and programming; for network labs and your own devices, it is too far removed from the hardware.

karten.v: What does “image” mean?
karten.r: An image is a file that contains the contents of an entire storage device sector by sector, with partition table, file systems and boot files.

karten.v: What does “ISO image” mean?
karten.r: An ISO image is an image in the format of a CD or DVD; it has the extension .iso.

karten.v: What does “checksum” mean?
karten.r: A checksum is a short value that a fixed method calculates from the contents of a file.

karten.v: What does “SHA-256” mean?
karten.r: The images of Linux distributions use the SHA-256 method, which is specified by the U.S.

karten.v: An ______ is an entire storage device in a single file.
karten.r: An image is an entire storage device in a single file.

karten.v: The ______ is the fingerprint of a file: same contents, same value; any change, a different value.
karten.r: The checksum is the fingerprint of a file: same contents, same value; any change, a different value.

karten.v: Compare ______ completely, preferably with sha256sum -c or with Get-FileHash and -eq.
karten.r: Compare checksums completely, preferably with sha256sum -c or with Get-FileHash and -eq.

karten.v: A ______ checksum proves that the file is unchanged, but not that it is genuine.
karten.r: A matching checksum proves that the file is unchanged, but not that it is genuine.

karten.v: What does “firmware” mean?
karten.r: The firmware is a program that is stored permanently in a memory chip on the main circuit board (the motherboard) and runs first when the computer is switched on.

karten.v: What does “UEFI” mean?
karten.r: Today's PCs use firmware following the UEFI standard (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface); its predecessor was called BIOS, and many people still call the firmware “BIOS” today.

karten.v: What does “boot order” mean?
karten.r: The boot order is the list of boot entries in the order in which the firmware tries them at power-on.

karten.v: What does “boot menu” mean?
karten.r: The boot menu is a selection that the firmware displays when you press a key at power-on; in it, you choose an entry once, without changing the boot order.

karten.v: What does “boot loader” mean?
karten.r: A boot loader is the boot program that the firmware loads and that in turn loads the kernel of the operating system into main memory and starts it.

karten.v: What does “GRUB” mean?
karten.r: Linux distributions usually use the GRUB boot loader.

karten.v: What does “BitLocker” mean?
karten.r: BitLocker is the drive encryption of Windows; in Windows Home, it is called device encryption.

karten.v: What does “recovery key” mean?
karten.r: If the boot chain has been changed, Windows demands the recovery key, a 48-digit number that was generated when the encryption was switched on.

karten.v: The ______ runs first after switching on and loads a boot program from the EFI system partition.
karten.r: The firmware runs first after switching on and loads a boot program from the EFI system partition.

karten.v: For a one-time ______ from the stick, you use the boot menu and leave the boot order as it is.
karten.r: For a one-time start from the stick, you use the boot menu and leave the boot order as it is.

karten.v: The ______ loads the boot loader, and the boot loader loads the kernel.
karten.r: The firmware loads the boot loader, and the boot loader loads the kernel.

karten.v: ______ starts only boot programs with a valid seal; it checks authenticity and encrypts nothing.
karten.r: Secure Boot starts only boot programs with a valid seal; it checks authenticity and encrypts nothing.

karten.v: Before you do anything to the boot chain, you back up the 48-digit ______.
karten.r: Before you do anything to the boot chain, you back up the 48-digit recovery key.

karten.v: If ______ is off, you switch on only this one setting in the firmware, with the recovery key backed up.
karten.r: If hardware virtualization is off, you switch on only this one setting in the firmware, with the recovery key backed up.

karten.v: A new VM with the checked ______, without unattended installation, with 6 GB of memory, 2 processors and a 25 GB disk.
karten.r: A new VM with the checked image, without unattended installation, with 6 GB of memory, 2 processors and a 25 GB disk.

karten.v: After the installation, create a ______ “sauber”; you can return to it at any time, but you lose everything that came later.
karten.r: After the installation, create a snapshot “sauber”; you can return to it at any time, but you lose everything that came later.

karten.v: Ctrl+Alt+T opens the ______ in Ubuntu; there, uname -r shows Ubuntu's kernel.
karten.r: Ctrl+Alt+T opens the terminal in Ubuntu; there, uname -r shows Ubuntu's kernel.

karten.v: What does “live system” mean?
karten.r: A live system is an operating system that starts and runs entirely from a removable storage device without mounting the computer's built-in storage devices.

karten.v: What does “overlay” mean?
karten.r: An overlay places two file systems on top of each other and shows them as one: a lower, read-only layer and an upper, writable layer.

karten.v: What does “persistence” mean?
karten.r: For a live system, persistence means that it stores changes not in main memory but in an additional storage area on the stick, so that they survive the restart.

karten.v: A ______ runs from the stick and from main memory and leaves the internal SSD alone.
karten.r: A live system runs from the stick and from main memory and leaves the internal SSD alone.

karten.v: ______ is a compressed file system that can only be read.
karten.r: squashfs is a compressed file system that can only be read.

karten.v: ______ is a file system in main memory, writable and volatile.
karten.r: tmpfs is a file system in main memory, writable and volatile.

karten.v: The ______ shows a read-only and a writable layer as one tree; all changes end up at the top.
karten.r: The overlay shows a read-only and a writable layer as one tree; all changes end up at the top.

karten.v: After switching off, everything you changed in the ______ is gone, and every start is fresh again.
karten.r: After switching off, everything you changed in the live system is gone, and every start is fresh again.

karten.v: ______ turns the stick into a system that remembers, but in Ubuntu, it is a poorly maintained add-on.
karten.r: Persistence turns the stick into a system that remembers, but in Ubuntu, it is a poorly maintained add-on.

karten.v: What does “writing tool” mean?
karten.r: A writing tool is a program that writes an image sector by sector onto an entire storage device.

karten.v: Go to the stick via “Restart”, not via “Shut down”, and do not ______ the Windows partitions in the live system.
karten.r: Go to the stick via “Restart”, not via “Shut down”, and do not touch the Windows partitions in the live system.

karten.v: Download the ______ and SHA256SUMS from Ubuntu, compare the checksum and continue only if the answer is True.
karten.r: Download the image and SHA256SUMS from Ubuntu, compare the checksum and continue only if the answer is True.

karten.v: A ______ such as balenaEtcher or Rufus turns the stick into a copy of the image; everything that was on it before is gone.
karten.r: A writing tool such as balenaEtcher or Rufus turns the stick into a copy of the image; everything that was on it before is gone.

karten.v: “Restart”, ______, the “UEFI” entry with the stick, “Try Ubuntu”, never “Install”.
karten.r: “Restart”, boot menu, the “UEFI” entry with the stick, “Try Ubuntu”, never “Install”.

karten.v: In the ______, lsblk shows the internal SSD without a mount point, that is, unused.
karten.r: In the live system, lsblk shows the internal SSD without a mount point, that is, unused.

karten.v: Switch off, unplug the stick, and Windows ______ as before; convert the stick back with the same care as when writing.
karten.r: Switch off, unplug the stick, and Windows starts as before; convert the stick back with the same care as when writing.

karten.v: What does “terminal emulator” mean?
karten.r: A terminal emulator is a program that shows a window with lines of text, passes each keystroke as a character to another program and displays in the window each character that this program sends back.

karten.v: What does “shell” mean?
karten.r: A shell is a program that accepts commands as text, runs them or has other programs run them, and then waits for the next command.

karten.v: What does “bash” mean?
karten.r: On Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora, the terminal opens the shell bash, short for “Bourne-Again Shell”.

karten.v: What does “current folder” mean?
karten.r: The shell always works in a particular folder. This folder is called the current folder.

karten.v: What does “root” mean?
karten.r: Every Linux system has a user account that may do anything: read anyone else's files, change system files, install programs. This account is called root.

karten.v: What does “session” mean?
karten.r: A session is the time from the start of a shell in a terminal until its end.

karten.v: The ______ is only the window: it passes on keystrokes and draws characters without understanding them.
karten.r: The terminal emulator is only the window: it passes on keystrokes and draws characters without understanding them.

karten.v: The ______ is the program that reads your commands and has them run; on Ubuntu, it is bash.
karten.r: The shell is the program that reads your commands and has them run; on Ubuntu, it is bash.

karten.v: The ______ shows the user, the computer and the current folder; $ means ordinary user, # means root.
karten.r: The prompt shows the user, the computer and the current folder; $ means ordinary user, # means root.

karten.v: Each ______ window has its own shell and thus its own session, which ends with exit.
karten.r: Each terminal window has its own shell and thus its own session, which ends with exit.

karten.v: What does “command line” mean?
karten.r: A command line is everything you type after the prompt before you press Enter.

karten.v: What does “words” mean?
karten.r: The shell splits it at spaces into words; several spaces in a row separate like a single one.

karten.v: What does “command” mean?
karten.r: The first word of a command line is the command: the name of what is to be run.

karten.v: What does “argument” mean?
karten.r: Every word of the command line after the command is an argument.

karten.v: What does “option” mean?
karten.r: An option is an argument that begins with a minus sign and determines how the command works.

karten.v: What does “short option” mean?
karten.r: A short option consists of a minus sign and a single letter, such as -r.

karten.v: What does “long option” mean?
karten.r: A long option begins with two minus signs followed by a whole word, such as --kernel-release.

karten.v: What does “option with a value” mean?
karten.r: An option with a value requires an additional piece of information, such as a number.

karten.v: The ______ splits every command line into words at the spaces.
karten.r: The shell splits every command line into words at the spaces.

karten.v: The first word of the line is the ______, and in its name every letter counts, including whether it is upper or lower case.
karten.r: The first word of the line is the command, and in its name every letter counts, including whether it is upper or lower case.

karten.v: The ______ after the command are its arguments; the shell passes them on in order, and the command decides what they mean.
karten.r: The words after the command are its arguments; the shell passes them on in order, and the command decides what they mean.

karten.v: ______ begin with a minus sign and set how a command works; short options can be bundled.
karten.r: Options begin with a minus sign and set how a command works; short options can be bundled.

karten.v: ______ begin with two minus signs and a whole word; they are longer but self-explanatory.
karten.r: Long options begin with two minus signs and a whole word; they are longer but self-explanatory.

karten.v: Some ______ require a value, which comes as the next word, is attached directly or follows an equals sign.
karten.r: Some options require a value, which comes as the next word, is attached directly or follows an equals sign.

karten.v: After --, every word is an ordinary ______, even if it begins with a minus sign.
karten.r: After --, every word is an ordinary argument, even if it begins with a minus sign.

karten.v: What does “program file” mean?
karten.r: A program file is a file that contains an executable program.

karten.v: What does “search path” mean?
karten.r: The search path is the list of folders in which the shell looks for a program file with the name of the command; it starts the first one it finds.

karten.v: What does “builtin command” mean?
karten.r: A builtin command is a command that the shell runs itself, without starting another program.

karten.v: What does “alias” mean?
karten.r: An alias is a name that the shell replaces with a stored text while reading a command line if the name stands at the start as a command.

karten.v: Most ______ are program files, files with an executable program in them.
karten.r: Most commands are program files, files with an executable program in them.

karten.v: The ______ looks for program files in the folders of the search path, one after another, and starts the first one that matches.
karten.r: The shell looks for program files in the folders of the search path, one after another, and starts the first one that matches.

karten.v: The ______ handles builtin commands itself; commands such as cd and exit, which change the shell itself, have to be built in.
karten.r: The shell handles builtin commands itself; commands such as cd and exit, which change the shell itself, have to be built in.

karten.v: An ______ is a shortcut that the shell replaces with a longer command before the search.
karten.r: An alias is a shortcut that the shell replaces with a longer command before the search.

karten.v: type says what the ______ does with a name; which only finds program files in the search path.
karten.r: type says what the shell does with a name; which only finds program files in the search path.

karten.v: What does “short help” mean?
karten.r: The short help is a brief description that a program outputs when you call it with the option --help.

karten.v: What does “help” mean?
karten.r: The builtin command help shows the instructions for the shell's builtin commands.

karten.v: What does “manual page” mean?
karten.r: A manual page, or man page for short, is the detailed description of a command, a file format, a system call or another part of the system, collected in the manual that every Linux comes with.

karten.v: What does “man” mean?
karten.r: The command man with the name as an argument displays it.

karten.v: What does “pager” mean?
karten.r: A pager is a program that shows a long text one screen at a time and lets you scroll and search in it.

karten.v: What does “sections” mean?
karten.r: The manual is divided into numbered sections, one for each kind of content (Table 3).

karten.v: What does “apropos” mean?
karten.r: The command apropos searches the names and short descriptions of all manual pages for a keyword and lists the hits with their section.

karten.v: command --help shows a program's ______ at a glance.
karten.r: command --help shows a program's options at a glance.

karten.v: For ______, you ask the shell: help name.
karten.r: For builtin commands, you ask the shell: help name.

karten.v: man name shows the complete instructions in a fixed layout; you read the usage under SYNOPSIS with the ______ of the characters [ ], | and ....
karten.r: man name shows the complete instructions in a fixed layout; you read the usage under SYNOPSIS with the help of the characters [ ], | and ....

karten.v: man shows its pages in the ______ less: the Space bar pages forward, / searches, q quits.
karten.r: man shows its pages in the pager less: the Space bar pages forward, / searches, q quits.

karten.v: apropos keyword ______ manual pages whose short description contains the keyword.
karten.r: apropos keyword finds manual pages whose short description contains the keyword.

karten.v: Name unknown: apropos; builtin: help; ______: --help for the overview, man for everything.
karten.r: Name unknown: apropos; builtin: help; program file: --help for the overview, man for everything.

karten.v: What does “Completion” mean?
karten.r: Completion finishes a partly typed word as soon as you press the Tab key.

karten.v: What does “history” mean?
karten.r: The history is the numbered list of recently typed command lines that the shell keeps in its memory.

karten.v: What does “reverse search” mean?
karten.r: The reverse search searches the history from the newest line to the oldest for the text you type; you start it with Ctrl+R.

karten.v: What does “Ctrl+C” mean?
karten.r: The key combination Ctrl+C asks the program that is currently running in the terminal to stop immediately; almost all programs then stop, and the shell shows the prompt again.

karten.v: What does “Ctrl+D” mean?
karten.r: The key combination Ctrl+D at the start of a line tells the program that is currently reading that no more input follows.

karten.v: What does “keyboard shortcut” mean?
karten.r: A keyboard shortcut of the command line is a key combination that the shell does not write into the line as a character but carries out as an instruction to edit the line or the window.

karten.v: The Tab key completes ______ and file names; pressed twice, it shows all the possibilities.
karten.r: The Tab key completes command and file names; pressed twice, it shows all the possibilities.

karten.v: The ______ remembers every line in the history; the Up arrow key and history bring it back.
karten.r: The shell remembers every line in the history; the Up arrow key and history bring it back.

karten.v: Ctrl+R searches backward in the ______ for what you type; Enter runs the hit.
karten.r: Ctrl+R searches backward in the history for what you type; Enter runs the hit.

karten.v: ______ interrupts the running program or discards the partly typed line.
karten.r: Ctrl+C interrupts the running program or discards the partly typed line.

karten.v: ______ tells the reading program “no more input”; on the empty command line, it ends the shell.
karten.r: Ctrl+D tells the reading program “no more input”; on the empty command line, it ends the shell.

karten.v: Ctrl+A and Ctrl+E jump to the ______ and the end, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+W delete parts of the line, Ctrl+L clears the window.
karten.r: Ctrl+A and Ctrl+E jump to the start and the end, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+W delete parts of the line, Ctrl+L clears the window.

karten.v: uname -a names the ______, the computer and the processor; the first line of /etc/os-release names the distribution.
karten.r: uname -a names the kernel, the computer and the processor; the first line of /etc/os-release names the distribution.

karten.v: whoami gives your name, id your user ID and your ______.
karten.r: whoami gives your name, id your user ID and your groups.

karten.v: free -h shows the main memory; the ______ that matters is available, not free.
karten.r: free -h shows the main memory; the column that matters is available, not free.

karten.v: df -h / shows the size, used space and free space of the ______ system; -h calculates in multiples of 1024, -H in multiples of 1000.
karten.r: df -h / shows the size, used space and free space of the file system; -h calculates in multiples of 1024, -H in multiples of 1000.

karten.v: What does “coreutils” mean?
karten.r: The coreutils (“core utilities”) are a collection of over a hundred basic commands for files, text and system information, including ls, cat, head, cp, uname, date and df.

karten.v: What does “prefix gnu” mean?
karten.r: Ubuntu 26.04 also installs the GNU implementation of the coreutils, under names with the prefix gnu: gnuls is GNU's ls, gnuuname its uname, gnudate its date and so on.

karten.v: The ______ are the collection of core commands; the classic implementation comes from the GNU project.
karten.r: The coreutils are the collection of core commands; the classic implementation comes from the GNU project.

karten.v: Ubuntu 26.04 uses uutils, a rewrite in Rust, for most core ______; --version shows which implementation answers.
karten.r: Ubuntu 26.04 uses uutils, a rewrite in Rust, for most core commands; --version shows which implementation answers.

karten.v: In Ubuntu 26.04, you reach the GNU implementation of each core ______ with the prefix gnu, for example gnuls.
karten.r: In Ubuntu 26.04, you reach the GNU implementation of each core command with the prefix gnu, for example gnuls.

karten.v: uutils and GNU deliver the same results but word ______ texts and error messages differently.
karten.r: uutils and GNU deliver the same results but word help texts and error messages differently.

karten.v: What does “file” mean?
karten.r: A file is a sequence of bytes that is stored permanently under a name.

karten.v: What does “directory” mean?
karten.r: A directory is a list of entries.

karten.v: What does “directory tree” mean?
karten.r: The directories of a Linux system form a single directory tree: every directory except one is entered under its name in exactly one other directory.

karten.v: What does “root directory” mean?
karten.r: The one directory that is not entered in any other is called the root directory; it is written as a single slash /.

karten.v: What does “parent directory” mean?
karten.r: The directory in which another one is entered is called its parent directory.

karten.v: What does “subdirectory” mean?
karten.r: Conversely, every directory that is entered in another one is a subdirectory of it.

karten.v: A ______ is a stored sequence of bytes with a name; what the bytes mean is decided by the program that reads them.
karten.r: A file is a stored sequence of bytes with a name; what the bytes mean is decided by the program that reads them.

karten.v: A ______ is a list that links names to files or to further directories.
karten.r: A directory is a list that links names to files or to further directories.

karten.v: All directories hang in a single ______ with the root /; further storage devices are mounted instead of getting a letter.
karten.r: All directories hang in a single tree with the root /; further storage devices are mounted instead of getting a letter.

karten.v: What does “working directory” mean?
karten.r: The working directory of a running program is the directory in which it is currently working.

karten.v: What does “path” mean?
karten.r: A path is a sequence of names, separated by slashes /, that describes the route through the directory tree to a file or a directory.

karten.v: What does “absolute path” mean?
karten.r: An absolute path begins with /.

karten.v: What does “relative path” mean?
karten.r: A relative path does not begin with /.

karten.v: What does “home directory” mean?
karten.r: A user's home directory is the directory that belongs to them for their own files.

karten.v: What does “tilde” mean?
karten.r: The abbreviation for it is the tilde ~: if it is at the beginning of a word, the shell replaces it with the path of your home directory before it starts the command.

karten.v: What does “cd” mean?
karten.r: The builtin command cd (short for “change directory”) makes the directory that its argument denotes the shell's new working directory.

karten.v: The ______ is the location in the tree to which commands without a location refer; pwd names it.
karten.r: The working directory is the location in the tree to which commands without a location refer; pwd names it.

karten.v: A ______ is a set of directions through the tree: names, separated by slashes.
karten.r: A path is a set of directions through the tree: names, separated by slashes.

karten.v: An ______ begins with / and is valid from everywhere.
karten.r: An absolute path begins with / and is valid from everywhere.

karten.v: A ______ begins without / and is valid from the working directory.
karten.r: A relative path begins without / and is valid from the working directory.

karten.v: . is the ______ itself, .. the parent directory; in the root, .. leads back to the root.
karten.r: . is the directory itself, .. the parent directory; in the root, .. leads back to the root.

karten.v: The ______ is your own place in the tree; ~ at the beginning of a word stands for its path.
karten.r: The home directory is your own place in the tree; ~ at the beginning of a word stands for its path.

karten.v: cd changes the ______: cd path goes there, cd goes home, cd - goes back, cd .. goes one level up.
karten.r: cd changes the working directory: cd path goes there, cd goes home, cd - goes back, cd .. goes one level up.

karten.v: What does “ls” mean?
karten.r: The command ls prints, for each directory given as an argument, the names of its entries, sorted by name, and for every other file its name.

karten.v: What does “hidden file” mean?
karten.r: A hidden file is a file or directory whose name begins with a dot.

karten.v: What does “regular file” mean?
karten.r: A - stands for a regular file, that is, a file with contents such as a text or a program; a d stands for a directory.

karten.v: What does “-h” mean?
karten.r: Together with -l, the option -h (short for “human-readable”) makes ls print each size in the largest suitable unit: K for 1024 bytes, M for $1024^2$ bytes, G for $1024^3$ bytes.

karten.v: ls lists the entries of directories; for a ______, it gives its name.
karten.r: ls lists the entries of directories; for a regular file, it gives its name.

karten.v: A name with a dot at the ______ makes a file invisible to the ordinary ls; ls -a shows everything.
karten.r: A name with a dot at the start makes a file invisible to the ordinary ls; ls -a shows everything.

karten.v: ls -l shows the type, permissions, owner, ______, size, modification time and name of each entry; -d shows the directory itself instead of its contents.
karten.r: ls -l shows the type, permissions, owner, group, size, modification time and name of each entry; -d shows the directory itself instead of its contents.

karten.v: -S ______ by size, -t by time, -r reverses, -R descends into all subdirectories.
karten.r: -S sorts by size, -t by time, -r reverses, -R descends into all subdirectories.

karten.v: ______ names may contain anything except / and distinguish between uppercase and lowercase; spaces and a dash at the start cause trouble, so you avoid them.
karten.r: File names may contain anything except / and distinguish between uppercase and lowercase; spaces and a dash at the start cause trouble, so you avoid them.

karten.v: What does “cat” mean?
karten.r: The command cat reads the files given as arguments in turn and writes out their bytes unchanged, one after the other.

karten.v: What does “less” mean?
karten.r: If less receives a file as an argument, it shows the file's contents page by page.

karten.v: What does “head, tail” mean?
karten.r: The command head writes out the first lines of a file, the command tail the last ones.

karten.v: cat writes out the contents of ______ one after the other; for short files, this is the quickest look inside.
karten.r: cat writes out the contents of files one after the other; for short files, this is the quickest look inside.

karten.v: less file shows a ______ page by page, with paging and search, without changing it.
karten.r: less file shows a file page by page, with paging and search, without changing it.

karten.v: head shows the beginning, tail the end of a ______, ten lines each or as many as -n says.
karten.r: head shows the beginning, tail the end of a file, ten lines each or as many as -n says.

karten.v: wc counts lines, ______ and bytes; -l, -w, -c select one of the numbers.
karten.r: wc counts lines, words and bytes; -l, -w, -c select one of the numbers.

karten.v: file determines the type of a ______ from its contents, regardless of name and extension.
karten.r: file determines the type of a file from its contents, regardless of name and extension.

karten.v: What does “mkdir” mean?
karten.r: The command mkdir (short for “make directory”) creates a new, empty directory for each argument.

karten.v: What does “-p” mean?
karten.r: The option -p (short for “parents”) also creates missing intermediate directories and reports no error if a directory already exists.

karten.v: What does “touch” mean?
karten.r: The command touch sets the time of the last modification and of the last access of each file named to the current time.

karten.v: What does “text editor” mean?
karten.r: A text editor is a program with which you create and change text files; it stores only the characters, no font and no formatting.

karten.v: touch creates an empty ______ or, for an existing one, only sets the modification time to now.
karten.r: touch creates an empty file or, for an existing one, only sets the modification time to now.

karten.v: nano file opens a ______ in the terminal; Ctrl+O saves, Ctrl+X quits.
karten.r: nano file opens a text editor in the terminal; Ctrl+O saves, Ctrl+X quits.

karten.v: What does “cp” mean?
karten.r: The command cp (short for “copy”) copies a file: cp source target creates a new file with the same contents under the name target.

karten.v: What does “-r” mean?
karten.r: With the option -r (short for “recursive”), cp copies a directory together with everything in it, level by level.

karten.v: What does “mv” mean?
karten.r: The command mv (short for “move”) gives a file or a directory a new name or a new location: mv source target renames source to target.

karten.v: What does “rm” mean?
karten.r: The command rm (short for “remove”) removes the named files from their directories, immediately and usually without asking.

karten.v: What does “rmdir” mean?
karten.r: The command rmdir (short for “remove directory”) removes a directory only if it is empty.

karten.v: What does “pattern” mean?
karten.r: A pattern is a word of the command line that contains one of the characters *, ? or [.

karten.v: cp source target creates an independent ______ and overwrites an existing target without asking; -i asks first.
karten.r: cp source target creates an independent copy and overwrites an existing target without asking; -i asks first.

karten.v: cp -r copies whole directories; if the target already exists, the ______ is created inside it.
karten.r: cp -r copies whole directories; if the target already exists, the copy is created inside it.

karten.v: mv renames or moves, depending on whether the target is an existing ______; an existing target is replaced without asking.
karten.r: mv renames or moves, depending on whether the target is an existing directory; an existing target is replaced without asking.

karten.v: rm deletes ______ immediately and permanently; rm -i asks first.
karten.r: rm deletes files immediately and permanently; rm -i asks first.

karten.v: ______ with *, ? and […] select many names at once; the shell replaces them with the matching names before the command starts.
karten.r: Patterns with *, ? and […] select many names at once; the shell replaces them with the matching names before the command starts.

karten.v: What does “Filesystem Hierarchy Standard” mean?
karten.r: The Filesystem Hierarchy Standard, FHS for short, specifies which directories a Linux system should have and which kind of files belongs in which of them.

karten.v: What does “/usr” mean?
karten.r: The directory /usr contains the programs, libraries and unchanging data that come with the distribution.

karten.v: What does “library” mean?
karten.r: A library is a file with program parts that many programs share instead of each containing them itself.

karten.v: What does “/etc” mean?
karten.r: The directory /etc contains the configuration that applies to the whole system.

karten.v: What does “/home” mean?
karten.r: The directory /home contains a home directory for each ordinary user, named after that user.

karten.v: What does “/root” mean?
karten.r: The home directory of root is kept apart from it in /root.

karten.v: What does “/var” mean?
karten.r: The directory /var (short for “variable”) contains data that change while the system is running.

karten.v: What does “log files” mean?
karten.r: An important part of it is /var/log with the log files: files to whose end a program continuously writes what happens, each entry with the date and time.

karten.v: What does “/tmp” mean?
karten.r: The directory /tmp is intended for temporary files.

karten.v: What does “device file” mean?
karten.r: A device file is an entry in the directory tree behind which there are no stored contents but a device that a driver in the kernel manages.

karten.v: What does “virtual file system” mean?
karten.r: A virtual file system is a file system whose files are not on any storage device; the kernel creates their contents at the moment a program reads them.

karten.v: The FHS specifies which ______ is there for what; that is why all Linux systems look alike in their basic outline.
karten.r: The FHS specifies which directory is there for what; that is why all Linux systems look alike in their basic outline.

karten.v: Under /usr is everything that the ______ brings along in programs and fixed data; your own add-on software belongs in /usr/local or /opt.
karten.r: Under /usr is everything that the distribution brings along in programs and fixed data; your own add-on software belongs in /usr/local or /opt.

karten.v: /etc is the place for the configuration of the whole system, in the form of text ______.
karten.r: /etc is the place for the configuration of the whole system, in the form of text files.

karten.v: /tmp is a shared place for short-lived ______; what is to stay belongs in the home directory.
karten.r: /tmp is a shared place for short-lived files; what is to stay belongs in the home directory.

karten.v: In /dev, devices appear as ______; you read and write them with the same tools as regular files.
karten.r: In /dev, devices appear as files; you read and write them with the same tools as regular files.

karten.v: /proc and /sys are windows into the ______: their files are created when they are read and reveal the uptime, the processor, the devices and the running programs.
karten.r: /proc and /sys are windows into the kernel: their files are created when they are read and reveal the uptime, the processor, the devices and the running programs.

karten.v: What does “inode” mean?
karten.r: An inode is the administrative record of a file in the file system.

karten.v: What does “hard link” mean?
karten.r: A hard link is a further directory entry for an existing inode, that is, an additional name for the same file.

karten.v: What does “link count” mean?
karten.r: The inode keeps count of how many entries point to it; this number is called the link count.

karten.v: What does “symbolic link” mean?
karten.r: A symbolic link is a file of its own of type l whose only contents are a path.

karten.v: What does “usr-merge” mean?
karten.r: The usr-merge, the merging of /usr, is the arrangement common today in which the directories /bin, /sbin and /lib are symbolic links to usr/bin, usr/sbin and usr/lib.

karten.v: The ______ is the administrative record of a file with all the information except the name; ls -i shows its number, stat its contents.
karten.r: The inode is the administrative record of a file with all the information except the name; ls -i shows its number, stat its contents.

karten.v: A ______ is a table of names and inode numbers; a file name is only an entry that points to an inode.
karten.r: A directory is a table of names and inode numbers; a file name is only an entry that points to an inode.

karten.v: A ______ is a second name for the same inode; the link count in the second column of ls -l counts the names.
karten.r: A hard link is a second name for the same inode; the link count in the second column of ls -l counts the names.

karten.v: rm removes a name; the ______ disappears only with its last name.
karten.r: rm removes a name; the file disappears only with its last name.

karten.v: A ______ is a small file with a path in it; it redirects accesses and can point nowhere if the target is missing.
karten.r: A symbolic link is a small file with a path in it; it redirects accesses and can point nowhere if the target is missing.

karten.v: /bin, /sbin and /lib are ______ to /usr today; old paths keep working.
karten.r: /bin, /sbin and /lib are symbolic links to /usr today; old paths keep working.

karten.v: A ______ is a name with equal rights for the same inode, only in the same file system and only for files; a symbolic link is a signpost that may point anywhere, even nowhere.
karten.r: A hard link is a name with equal rights for the same inode, only in the same file system and only for files; a symbolic link is a signpost that may point anywhere, even nowhere.

karten.v: What does “findmnt” mean?
karten.r: The command findmnt lists the mounted file systems with mount point (TARGET), source (SOURCE), type (FSTYPE) and options (OPTIONS).

karten.v: What does “df” mean?
karten.r: If df receives paths as arguments, it shows for each path the file system in which it is located, with size, used and free space.

karten.v: What does “/mnt/c” mean?
karten.r: Under WSL 2, the Windows drive C: is mounted at /mnt/c, as a file system of type 9p.

karten.v: findmnt shows which ______ system is mounted at which directory; findmnt -T path answers the question for a single path.
karten.r: findmnt shows which file system is mounted at which directory; findmnt -T path answers the question for a single path.

karten.v: df -hT path shows the type, size and free space of the ______ system in which a path is located.
karten.r: df -hT path shows the type, size and free space of the file system in which a path is located.

karten.v: Under WSL 2, /mnt/c is a ______ system of its own with the rules of Windows; for Linux work, everything belongs in the home directory.
karten.r: Under WSL 2, /mnt/c is a file system of its own with the rules of Windows; for Linux work, everything belongs in the home directory.

karten.v: What does “find” mean?
karten.r: The command find walks through the subtree below each given starting directory, entry by entry and level by level.

karten.v: What does “-type type” mean?
karten.r: The test -type type passes if an entry is of the given type: f for a regular file, d for a directory, l for a symbolic link, b and c for device files.

karten.v: What does “-size n” mean?
karten.r: The test -size n compares the size of an entry with n; +n means greater than n, -n less than n, and n alone exactly n.

karten.v: What does “-mtime n” mean?
karten.r: The test -mtime n compares the age of the last modification in whole days of 24 hours with n; partial days are dropped, and +n and -n mean more and less, as with -size.

karten.v: What does “!” mean?
karten.r: A ! in front of a test negates it.

karten.v: What does “-maxdepth n” mean?
karten.r: The option -maxdepth n directly after the starting directories limits the search to n levels below the starting directory.

karten.v: What does “action” mean?
karten.r: What find does with a match is determined by an action; if none is given, it is -print, which prints the path.

karten.v: What does “du” mean?
karten.r: The command du (short for “disk usage”) adds up, for each given directory and each subdirectory in it, the space that the files occupy on the storage device, in units of 1024 bytes.

karten.v: find start tests walks through a subtree and prints the ______ of the entries that pass all tests.
karten.r: find start tests walks through a subtree and prints the paths of the entries that pass all tests.

karten.v: -name "pattern" searches by name; the quotes make sure that find, not the ______, applies the pattern.
karten.r: -name "pattern" searches by name; the quotes make sure that find, not the shell, applies the pattern.

karten.v: -type f, -type d and -type l select ______, directories or symbolic links.
karten.r: -type f, -type d and -type l select regular files, directories or symbolic links.

karten.v: -mtime and -mmin search by age in whole days or minutes, -newer by comparison with another ______.
karten.r: -mtime and -mmin search by age in whole days or minutes, -newer by comparison with another file.

karten.v: du -sh shows how much space a ______ occupies; whole blocks are counted, which is why even a tiny file occupies 4 KiB.
karten.r: du -sh shows how much space a directory occupies; whole blocks are counted, which is why even a tiny file occupies 4 KiB.

karten.v: What does “process ID” mean?
karten.r: The kernel keeps each process separate from all others. It gives each process a number, the process ID.

karten.v: What does “stream” mean?
karten.r: A stream is a sequence of bytes that a process reads or writes in order.

karten.v: What does “end of the stream” mean?
karten.r: If nothing more arrives during reading and nothing more can arrive, the end of the stream has been reached; the kernel tells the reading process by having a read request return zero bytes.

karten.v: What does “Standard input” mean?
karten.r: Standard input (stdin for short) is the stream from which a process reads when it is not told otherwise.

karten.v: What does “Standard output” mean?
karten.r: Standard output (stdout for short) is the stream to which a process writes its results.

karten.v: What does “Standard error” mean?
karten.r: Standard error (stderr for short) is a second output stream to which a process writes error messages, warnings and notices.

karten.v: What does “file descriptor” mean?
karten.r: A file descriptor, descriptor for short, is a small integer under which the kernel keeps track of an open file for a process.

karten.v: A program is a ______; a process is a running execution of it, with its own memory, its own open files, its own working directory and its own number.
karten.r: A program is a file; a process is a running execution of it, with its own memory, its own open files, its own working directory and its own number.

karten.v: A ______ is a sequence of bytes that a process reads or writes in order without knowing where they come from; when a read request returns zero bytes, the stream has ended.
karten.r: A stream is a sequence of bytes that a process reads or writes in order without knowing where they come from; when a read request returns zero bytes, the stream has ended.

karten.v: ______ is the way in to a process; in the terminal it is the keyboard, and Ctrl+D ends the stream.
karten.r: Standard input is the way in to a process; in the terminal it is the keyboard, and Ctrl+D ends the stream.

karten.v: ______ is the way out for the results of a process; in the terminal it ends up on the screen.
karten.r: Standard output is the way out for the results of a process; in the terminal it ends up on the screen.

karten.v: ______ is a separate way out for messages; in the terminal it mixes with standard output.
karten.r: Standard error is a separate way out for messages; in the terminal it mixes with standard output.

karten.v: A descriptor is the number by which a ______ refers to an open file when dealing with the kernel; 0, 1 and 2 are the three standard streams.
karten.r: A descriptor is the number by which a process refers to an open file when dealing with the kernel; 0, 1 and 2 are the three standard streams.

karten.v: What does “redirection” mean?
karten.r: A redirection is an instruction to the shell to connect a descriptor of the new process to a different file before the program starts.

karten.v: What does “appending” mean?
karten.r: The notation command >> file connects standard output to the file for appending: every byte written goes after the existing contents, and nothing is deleted.

karten.v: What does “copy” mean?
karten.r: The notation n>&m makes descriptor $n$ a copy of descriptor $m$: afterward, $n$ leads to the same open file as $m$ at that moment.

karten.v: command > file sends ______ into a file that the shell creates or empties beforehand; the program notices nothing of this.
karten.r: command > file sends standard output into a file that the shell creates or empties beforehand; the program notices nothing of this.

karten.v: >> appends ______ to a file without touching the old contents.
karten.r: >> appends standard output to a file without touching the old contents.

karten.v: 2> redirects ______; a number in front of > selects the descriptor.
karten.r: 2> redirects standard error; a number in front of > selects the descriptor.

karten.v: 2>&1 makes the error output lead to where ______ currently leads; &> is the short form for both ways out into one file.
karten.r: 2>&1 makes the error output lead to where standard output currently leads; &> is the short form for both ways out into one file.

karten.v: ______ take effect from left to right; 2>&1 copies the target that 1 has at that moment, which is why it goes after > file.
karten.r: Redirections take effect from left to right; 2>&1 copies the target that 1 has at that moment, which is why it goes after > file.

karten.v: Never read from a ______ and write with > into the same file; the shell empties it before the program can read it.
karten.r: Never read from a file and write with > into the same file; the shell empties it before the program can read it.

karten.v: What does “here document” mean?
karten.r: A here document is a redirection of the form command <<ENDMARKER, followed by lines of text and finally a line that contains only the end marker.

karten.v: What does “here string” mean?
karten.r: A here string is a redirection of the form command <<< "text".

karten.v: command < file makes a ______ the standard input; the program reads a stream and does not know the name.
karten.r: command < file makes a file the standard input; the program reads a stream and does not know the name.

karten.v: A ______ gives a command the following lines, up to the end marker, as standard input.
karten.r: A here document gives a command the following lines, up to the end marker, as standard input.

karten.v: A ______ gives a command one line of text as standard input, with a line end appended.
karten.r: A here string gives a command one line of text as standard input, with a line end appended.

karten.v: What does “pipe” mean?
karten.r: A pipe connects the standard output of one process to the standard input of another.

karten.v: What does “filter” mean?
karten.r: A filter is a program that reads data from its standard input, transforms it and writes the result to its standard output.

karten.v: What does “pipeline” mean?
karten.r: A pipeline is a sequence of commands connected by |.

karten.v: What does “tee” mean?
karten.r: The command tee reads its standard input and writes everything it reads both to its standard output and to every file named as an argument.

karten.v: What does “Unix philosophy” mean?
karten.r: The Unix philosophy is a principle for building programs.

karten.v: command1 | command2 connects the ______ of the first program to the standard input of the second; both run at the same time, and the messages still go to the screen.
karten.r: command1 | command2 connects the standard output of the first program to the standard input of the second; both run at the same time, and the messages still go to the screen.

karten.v: A ______ reads its standard input, transforms it and writes the result to its standard output; that is why it fits behind a pipe.
karten.r: A filter reads its standard input, transforms it and writes the result to its standard output; that is why it fits behind a pipe.

karten.v: A ______ lines up filters like the stations of an assembly line; each station works with what the previous one delivers.
karten.r: A pipeline lines up filters like the stations of an assembly line; each station works with what the previous one delivers.

karten.v: tee file passes its input on unchanged and at the same time writes a ______ into the file.
karten.r: tee file passes its input on unchanged and at the same time writes a copy into the file.

karten.v: Every ______ ends with a number from 0 to 255; 0 means success, and $? returns the number of the most recently ended command.
karten.r: Every process ends with a number from 0 to 255; 0 means success, and $? returns the number of the most recently ended command.

karten.v: The nonzero number says which failure it was; what it means is stated in the program's ______.
karten.r: The nonzero number says which failure it was; what it means is stated in the program's manual page.

karten.v: 127 means “not found”, 126 “not executable”, and $128 + n$ means “ended by interrupt message $n$”, such as 130 after ______.
karten.r: 127 means “not found”, 126 “not executable”, and $128 + n$ means “ended by interrupt message $n$”, such as 130 after Ctrl+C.

karten.v: What does “AND list” mean?
karten.r: The notation command1 && command2 is an AND list: the shell runs command2 only if command1 ended with exit status 0. The exit status of the AND list is that of the last command executed.

karten.v: What does “OR list” mean?
karten.r: The notation command1 || command2 is an OR list: the shell runs command2 only if command1 ended with a nonzero exit status.

karten.v: The semicolon runs ______ one after another without paying attention to whether they succeed.
karten.r: The semicolon runs commands one after another without paying attention to whether they succeed.

karten.v: command1 && command2 runs the second ______ only if the first one succeeded.
karten.r: command1 && command2 runs the second command only if the first one succeeded.

karten.v: command1 || command2 runs the second ______ only if the first one failed.
karten.r: command1 || command2 runs the second command only if the first one failed.

karten.v: A ______ has the exit status of its last command; PIPESTATUS shows all of them, and pipefail makes earlier errors count as well.
karten.r: A pipeline has the exit status of its last command; PIPESTATUS shows all of them, and pipefail makes earlier errors count as well.

karten.v: What does “xargs” mean?
karten.r: The command xargs reads its standard input and splits it into words at spaces, tabs and line ends.

karten.v: What does “argument list limit” mean?
karten.r: The kernel limits how many bytes all the arguments of a program start may have together; getconf ARG_MAX shows this argument list limit.

karten.v: What comes through a ______ is input, not an argument; programs without input do not see it, and filters take it for data.
karten.r: What comes through a pipe is input, not an argument; programs without input do not see it, and filters take it for data.

karten.v: xargs command turns the ______ of its standard input into arguments for the command.
karten.r: xargs command turns the words of its standard input into arguments for the command.

karten.v: There is an upper limit for the ______ of a program start; xargs distributes the words over several calls on its own, and with -n in batches of a fixed size.
karten.r: There is an upper limit for the arguments of a program start; xargs distributes the words over several calls on its own, and with -n in batches of a fixed size.

karten.v: find … -exec command {} + passes the ______ directly as arguments to a command, names with spaces included; with \; instead of +, one at a time.
karten.r: find … -exec command {} + passes the matches directly as arguments to a command, names with spaces included; with \; instead of +, one at a time.

karten.v: What does “Expansion” mean?
karten.r: Expansion is the step in which the shell replaces certain parts of the words of a command line with other text.

karten.v: What does “Pathname expansion” mean?
karten.r: Pathname expansion is the expansion that replaces a pattern with the names of the existing files and directories that it matches; each match becomes a word of its own.

karten.v: What does “Brace expansion” mean?
karten.r: Brace expansion turns a word with curly braces into several words.

karten.v: What does “Tilde expansion” mean?
karten.r: Tilde expansion replaces a tilde at the beginning of a word.

karten.v: During ______, the shell rewrites parts of the command line before the program starts; the program sees only the result.
karten.r: During expansion, the shell rewrites parts of the command line before the program starts; the program sees only the result.

karten.v: ______ replaces a pattern with the sorted names that match it, in paths as well; no pattern character stands for a slash.
karten.r: Pathname expansion replaces a pattern with the sorted names that match it, in paths as well; no pattern character stands for a slash.

karten.v: A ______ captures hidden files only if it itself has a dot at this position; . and .. are never among the matches.
karten.r: A pattern captures hidden files only if it itself has a dot at this position; . and .. are never among the matches.

karten.v: With no ______, a pattern stays as it was typed, and the program receives it literally.
karten.r: With no match, a pattern stays as it was typed, and the program receives it literally.

karten.v: ______ creates several words from a list or sequence in curly braces, in the written order and without looking at files.
karten.r: Brace expansion creates several words from a list or sequence in curly braces, in the written order and without looking at files.

karten.v: ______ replaces a tilde at the beginning of a word with a home directory, your own or that of the named user.
karten.r: Tilde expansion replaces a tilde at the beginning of a word with a home directory, your own or that of the named user.

karten.v: What does “shell variable” mean?
karten.r: A shell variable is a name under which the running shell stores a text, the value of the variable.

karten.v: What does “assignment” mean?
karten.r: You create a variable or change its value with an assignment of the form NAME=value; there is no space before or after the equals sign.

karten.v: What does “Parameter expansion” mean?
karten.r: Parameter expansion replaces $NAME or ${NAME} with the value of the variable.

karten.v: What does “parameter” mean?
karten.r: In general, anything that stores a value which the shell inserts with a preceding dollar sign is called a parameter.

karten.v: What does “Command substitution” mean?
karten.r: Command substitution $(command) executes the command in the parentheses in a separate process and replaces itself with that command's standard output.

karten.v: What does “Arithmetic expansion” mean?
karten.r: Arithmetic expansion $((expression)) computes the expression in the double parentheses with integers and inserts the result as text.

karten.v: A ______ stores a text under a name; NAME=value without spaces stores it.
karten.r: A shell variable stores a text under a name; NAME=value without spaces stores it.

karten.v: $(command) inserts the output of a ______ into the command line, without the line ends at the end.
karten.r: $(command) inserts the output of a command into the command line, without the line ends at the end.

karten.v: What does “printf” mean?
karten.r: The builtin command printf writes text according to a format, its first argument.

karten.v: What does “Word splitting” mean?
karten.r: Word splitting splits the results of parameter expansion, command substitution and arithmetic expansion into separate words, provided these expansions were not within double quotes.

karten.v: What does “Quoting” mean?
karten.r: Quoting means marking characters of a command line so that the shell takes them literally instead of giving them a special meaning.

karten.v: What does “backslash” mean?
karten.r: A backslash \ outside of quotes removes the special meaning of the character directly after it.

karten.v: printf "[%s]\n" writes each ______ in brackets on a line of its own and thus makes visible which arguments a command receives.
karten.r: printf "[%s]\n" writes each argument in brackets on a line of its own and thus makes visible which arguments a command receives.

karten.v: ______ splits the results of expansions without double quotes at spaces, tabs and line ends; after that, pattern characters in them take effect as well.
karten.r: Word splitting splits the results of expansions without double quotes at spaces, tabs and line ends; after that, pattern characters in them take effect as well.

karten.v: ______ marks characters that the shell is to take literally; there are single and double quotes and the backslash.
karten.r: Quoting marks characters that the shell is to take literally; there are single and double quotes and the backslash.

karten.v: Between double quotes, the ______ inserts values with $ but does not split them, and it does not evaluate patterns, tildes or braces.
karten.r: Between double quotes, the shell inserts values with $ but does not split them, and it does not evaluate patterns, tildes or braces.

karten.v: The ______ protects exactly one character; at the end of a line, it continues the command line on the next line.
karten.r: The backslash protects exactly one character; at the end of a line, it continues the command line on the next line.

karten.v: At the end, the ______ removes the typed quotes and backslashes and joins the pieces of a word; quotes from values remain ordinary characters.
karten.r: At the end, the shell removes the typed quotes and backslashes and joins the pieces of a word; quotes from values remain ordinary characters.

karten.v: ______ belong in double quotes, text for programs in single quotes; otherwise a value can turn into several arguments.
karten.r: Expansions belong in double quotes, text for programs in single quotes; otherwise a value can turn into several arguments.

karten.v: Splitting, braces, then ______, parameters, arithmetic expansion and command substitution from left to right, then word splitting, patterns and finally quote removal.
karten.r: Splitting, braces, then tilde, parameters, arithmetic expansion and command substitution from left to right, then word splitting, patterns and finally quote removal.

karten.v: What does “child process” mean?
karten.r: If a process starts another one, the new process is a child process of the first.

karten.v: What does “parent process” mean?
karten.r: The starting process is called its parent process.

karten.v: What does “environment” mean?
karten.r: The environment of a process is a list of texts of the form NAME=value that the process receives when it starts, in addition to its arguments.

karten.v: What does “environment variable” mean?
karten.r: An environment variable is a shell variable that is marked for passing on; the shell writes all marked variables into the environment of every child process.

karten.v: What does “export” mean?
karten.r: The builtin command export marks a variable: export NAME marks an existing one, export NAME=value assigns and marks in one step.

karten.v: What does “env” mean?
karten.r: The command env starts a command with a modified environment.

karten.v: A ______ that another process starts is its child process; it does not automatically receive the shell's variables.
karten.r: A process that another process starts is its child process; it does not automatically receive the shell's variables.

karten.v: The ______ is a list of entries NAME=value that every process receives when it starts; printenv shows it.
karten.r: The environment is a list of entries NAME=value that every process receives when it starts; printenv shows it.

karten.v: export marks a ______ as an environment variable; every child receives it in its environment.
karten.r: export marks a shell variable as an environment variable; every child receives it in its environment.

karten.v: A child inherits a ______ of the environment; it can change the copy but cannot pass anything back.
karten.r: A child inherits a copy of the environment; it can change the copy but cannot pass anything back.

karten.v: NAME=value command gives only this ______ a setting of its own; the shell stays unchanged.
karten.r: NAME=value command gives only this command a setting of its own; the shell stays unchanged.

karten.v: printenv shows the ______, env starts a command with a modified or empty environment.
karten.r: printenv shows the environment, env starts a command with a modified or empty environment.

karten.v: PATH is the ______ as text, the directories separated by colons and in the order of the search.
karten.r: PATH is the search path as text, the directories separated by colons and in the order of the search.

karten.v: Without a slash, the ______ searches in PATH and takes the first match; with a slash, it starts exactly the named file.
karten.r: Without a slash, the shell searches in PATH and takes the first match; with a slash, it starts exactly the named file.

karten.v: The ______ is not part of the search path; you start a program there with ./.
karten.r: The working directory is not part of the search path; you start a program there with ./.

karten.v: PATH="directory:$PATH" puts a ______ of your own at the front of the search path; at the front means priority, and the old value must be kept.
karten.r: PATH="directory:$PATH" puts a directory of your own at the front of the search path; at the front means priority, and the old value must be kept.

karten.v: What does “startup file” mean?
karten.r: A startup file is a text file with commands for the shell that the shell reads and runs when it starts, as if you had typed the lines.

karten.v: What does “source” mean?
karten.r: The builtin command source file reads the file and runs its lines in the running shell, as if you had typed them.

karten.v: What does “login shell” mean?
karten.r: A login shell is a shell that starts at a login, for example after a user name and password on a text console, for a connection from another computer or when you open the WSL terminal.

karten.v: A ______ contains commands that the shell runs every time it starts; a new interactive bash reads ~/.bashrc.
karten.r: A startup file contains commands that the shell runs every time it starts; a new interactive bash reads ~/.bashrc.

karten.v: source file runs a ______ in the running shell; its settings remain because no child process comes into being.
karten.r: source file runs a file in the running shell; its settings remain because no child process comes into being.

karten.v: A ______ reads /etc/profile and ~/.profile, which on Ubuntu reads in ~/.bashrc; an interactive shell without a login reads only ~/.bashrc.
karten.r: A login shell reads /etc/profile and ~/.profile, which on Ubuntu reads in ~/.bashrc; an interactive shell without a login reads only ~/.bashrc.

karten.v: alias name='text' defines an abbreviation for the running interactive ______; it becomes permanent in ~/.bashrc.
karten.r: alias name='text' defines an abbreviation for the running interactive shell; it becomes permanent in ~/.bashrc.

karten.v: What does “record” mean?
karten.r: A record is a line of a text file that contains the values of one table row.

karten.v: What does “separator” mean?
karten.r: Between any two fields there is an agreed character, the separator.

karten.v: What does “column” mean?
karten.r: The fields with the same number in all records together form a column.

karten.v: What does “CSV file” mean?
karten.r: A CSV file is a text file in which each line is a record and the comma separates the fields.

karten.v: What does “header line” mean?
karten.r: Often the first line contains the names of the columns instead of values; it is called the header line.

karten.v: What does “carriage return” mean?
karten.r: The carriage return is an invisible character with the value 13, often written \r in programs.

karten.v: A line with the values of a table row is a ______; its values are the fields, separated by a separator and counted from the left.
karten.r: A line with the values of a table row is a record; its values are the fields, separated by a separator and counted from the left.

karten.v: A ______ is a table as text with one record per line and commas between the fields; the first line often names the columns.
karten.r: A CSV file is a table as text with one record per line and commas between the fields; the first line often names the columns.

karten.v: Windows ends lines with a ______ and a newline; under Linux, the invisible carriage return becomes the last character of every line, and cat -A shows it as ^M.
karten.r: Windows ends lines with a carriage return and a newline; under Linux, the invisible carriage return becomes the last character of every line, and cat -A shows it as ^M.

karten.v: tail -n +K ______ at line $K$, head -n -K stops $K$ lines before the end; tail -n +2 removes a header line.
karten.r: tail -n +K starts at line $K$, head -n -K stops $K$ lines before the end; tail -n +2 removes a header line.

karten.v: tail -f shows the end of a ______ and then everything that is appended, until Ctrl+C.
karten.r: tail -f shows the end of a file and then everything that is appended, until Ctrl+C.

karten.v: What does “cut” mean?
karten.r: The command cut writes out only selected parts of each line of its input.

karten.v: What does “tr” mean?
karten.r: The command tr reads its standard input character by character and writes it out changed.

karten.v: What does “paste” mean?
karten.r: The command paste reads several files at the same time and writes the first line of each file side by side in one line, then the second lines and so on.

karten.v: paste puts lines of several ______ side by side, paste -s puts all lines of a file into one line, with -d setting the separator.
karten.r: paste puts lines of several files side by side, paste -s puts all lines of a file into one line, with -d setting the separator.

karten.v: What does “sort” mean?
karten.r: The command sort reads all lines of its input and writes them out in order.

karten.v: What does “sort key” mean?
karten.r: -k A,B makes the fields from number $A$ to number $B$ the sort key: sort compares only this piece of the line.

karten.v: What does “locale” mean?
karten.r: The locale, the language setting, is a set of rules for a language and a country.

karten.v: What does “uniq” mean?
karten.r: The command uniq compares each line of its input with the line directly before it and, of several identical lines in a row, writes out only one.

karten.v: sort -t, -k3,3n ______ whole lines by the value of field 3; further -k decide in the case of a tie.
karten.r: sort -t, -k3,3n sorts whole lines by the value of field 3; further -k decide in the case of a tie.

karten.v: The ______ determines how sort orders; C and C.UTF-8 order by character numbers, and LC_ALL=C sort makes a result the same on every computer.
karten.r: The locale determines how sort orders; C and C.UTF-8 order by character numbers, and LC_ALL=C sort makes a result the same on every computer.

karten.v: What does “nl” mean?
karten.r: The command nl writes out each line of its input with a running number in front of it, separated by a tab.

karten.v: What does “seq” mean?
karten.r: The command seq writes a sequence of numbers, one per line.

karten.v: What does “diff” mean?
karten.r: The command diff compares two text files line by line and outputs what you would have to change in the first one to get the second one.

karten.v: diff a b uses a, c and d to show which lines you would have to add, change or delete in a to get b; the ______ tells whether there are differences.
karten.r: diff a b uses a, c and d to show which lines you would have to add, change or delete in a to get b; the exit status tells whether there are differences.

karten.v: What does “grep” mean?
karten.r: After the options, the command grep receives a search text as its first argument and then files.

karten.v: grep searchtext file writes the lines that contain the search text; the ______ tells whether there were any.
karten.r: grep searchtext file writes the lines that contain the search text; the exit status tells whether there were any.

karten.v: grep -o writes only the ______ pieces, one per line; with wc -l, you thus count matches instead of lines.
karten.r: grep -o writes only the matching pieces, one per line; with wc -l, you thus count matches instead of lines.

karten.v: With several ______, grep names the origin of each line; -r searches whole directory trees, -l names only the file names.
karten.r: With several files, grep names the origin of each line; -r searches whole directory trees, -l names only the file names.

karten.v: What does “string” mean?
karten.r: A string here is simply a sequence of characters, such as a word, a number or a whole line.

karten.v: What does “regular expression” mean?
karten.r: A regular expression is a text that describes a set of strings.

karten.v: What does “match” mean?
karten.r: A line matches a regular expression if a contiguous piece of it belongs to this set; this piece is called the match.

karten.v: What does “dot” mean?
karten.r: The dot . in a regular expression matches any single character.

karten.v: What does “bracket expression” mean?
karten.r: A bracket expression is a list of characters in square brackets; it matches exactly one character that is in the list.

karten.v: What does “character class” mean?
karten.r: A character class is a named group of characters that you write inside a bracket expression as [:name:].

karten.v: What does “anchor” mean?
karten.r: An anchor matches not a character but a position in the line.

karten.v: A ______ describes a set of strings; a line matches if a piece of it belongs to the set, and on the command line the expression stands in single quotes.
karten.r: A regular expression describes a set of strings; a line matches if a piece of it belongs to the set, and on the command line the expression stands in single quotes.

karten.v: […] ______ exactly one character from the list, [^…] exactly one that is not in it; a-z in the list is a range.
karten.r: […] matches exactly one character from the list, [^…] exactly one that is not in it; a-z in the list is a range.

karten.v: [[:digit:]], [[:alpha:]] and their relatives select characters by kind; the ______ determines what belongs to them.
karten.r: [[:digit:]], [[:alpha:]] and their relatives select characters by kind; the locale determines what belongs to them.

karten.v: ^ ______ an expression at the start of the line, $ at the end of the line; both match positions, not characters.
karten.r: ^ anchors an expression at the start of the line, $ at the end of the line; both match positions, not characters.

karten.v: What does “star” mean?
karten.r: A star * after an ordinary character, a dot or a bracket expression matches any number of repetitions of it in a row, including none at all.

karten.v: What does “basic form” mean?
karten.r: The basic form of regular expressions is the notation that grep uses without an option; it is called “basic regular expressions”, BRE for short.

karten.v: What does “extended form” mean?
karten.r: In the extended form, called “extended regular expressions”, ERE for short, they are special characters as well; grep -E turns it on.

karten.v: What does “quantifier” mean?
karten.r: A quantifier stands after an element of an expression and determines how often the element may occur in a row.
